tapeLine: Thursday 19 November: S&P 500 about −2% to 7,175.83, a sixth straight loss and the longest losing streak since 2024, 8.2% below last month’s record; Dow −1,101.11 (−2.2%) to 49,097.06; Nasdaq Composite −550.69 (−2.3%) to 23,879.20. More than 90% of S&P 500 members fell (AP via ABC News / Washington Post, 19 Nov).
matters:
The Anthropic debut did not lift the AI trade: stocks hit their session lows as ANT began trading, and the Dow closed below 50,000 for the first time since June (CNBC, 19 Nov). ANT opened at $111.50, ranged $92.72–$115.10 and closed at $97.17, about 17% above its $83 IPO price (Forbes; Bloomberg, 19 Nov). Nvidia, Micron, Microsoft and Meta gave up early gains, and a Hunterbrook short report on AMD added pressure (CNBC, 19 Nov).

Data were soft on activity and firm on prices: the Philadelphia Fed index fell to 6.3 from 20.9 against roughly 20 expected, with prices received at their highest since June 2022; initial claims rose to 203,000 against about 197–198K expected (Admiral Markets; MLQ, 19 Nov). Walmart beat on revenue ($188.8B) and adjusted EPS ($0.65) and raised its full-year EPS range to $2.84–$2.89, but shares fell about 1.9% premarket (Walmart 8-K; Investing.com, 19 Nov). Early Friday, Nasdaq-100 futures were down roughly 1–1.4% and S&P futures 0.2–0.6%, with the Nikkei and Kospi down more than 4% (CNBC; Yahoo Finance; TipRanks, 20 Nov).

alsoOnTape: 10-year Treasury yield about 5.06% Thursday (Investing.com historical 5.058%, −0.16%; Trading Economics 5.08%, 19 Nov); 10s–2s spread 0.28 pp (FRED, 19 Nov). Dollar index cited near 103.7–103.9. Oil and gold snapshots conflict in direction and level and are left out.
overnight: Latest confirmed close — Thursday 19 November: S&P 500 7,175.83 (about −2%); Nasdaq Composite 23,879.20 (−2.3%); Dow 49,097.06 (−1,101.11, −2.2%) (AP via ABC News, 19 Nov).

Anthropic (ANT) — first trade $111.50, close $97.17 (+17% vs $83 IPO); after-hours $92.60 reported by StockTitan. Market-value estimates differ by basis ($1.27–1.28T per Forbes/StockTitan; about $1.77T per Bloomberg) and are noted, not reconciled (19 Nov). Cryptoticker gives a $110.00 open, conflicting with the others.

Walmart — fiscal Q3 revenue $188.8B, adj. EPS $0.65 vs $0.64 expected; FY adj. EPS guidance raised to $2.84–$2.89; shares −1.92% premarket to $124.91. Closing move not confirmed (Walmart 8-K; Investing.com, 19 Nov).

Futures and Asia — early Friday 20 Nov: Nasdaq-100 futures down about 1–1.4%, S&P 500 futures down 0.2–0.6%, Dow futures roughly flat; Nikkei and Kospi down more than 4% early (CNBC; Yahoo Finance; TipRanks, 20 Nov). Snapshots vary by time.
macro: Philadelphia Fed manufacturing, November — 6.3 from 20.9, against about 20 expected; a six-month low. New orders −0.4; prices paid and received rose sharply, prices received highest since June 2022 (Admiral Markets; MLQ; Goldman summary via KuCoin, 19 Nov).

Initial jobless claims, week ending 14 Nov — 203,000, up 1,000 from a revised 202,000, above a ~197–198K consensus. Continuing claims rose to 1.763M, highest since early September; Goldman attributed much of that to a Michigan system change (MLQ; Admiral Markets, 19 Nov).
flow: Breadth, dealer gamma, put-call and skew are paid data and are not on this page. AP reported more than 90% of S&P 500 stocks fell Thursday (19 Nov).

regime.tag: Six straight S&P 500 losses, the Dow under 50,000 and the Nasdaq down about 5% on the week, with the Anthropic debut failing to act as a clearing event.
regime.sizing: Whether Friday’s weaker Nasdaq futures and the 4% Asian declines carry into the week’s close is unresolved.

secondOrder: Thursday reversed Wednesday’s split: the Nasdaq led the decline after having held up the day before, and the selling hit even names described as defensive AI bets such as Alphabet and Amazon (CNBC, 19 Nov). The Philly Fed showed falling orders alongside rising prices paid and received, the combination the October minutes flagged. Observations, not forecasts.

scorecard.text: The prior brief reported Nasdaq-100 futures up about 2% and S&P futures up about 1.1% early Thursday on the Anthropic pricing. The Nasdaq Composite closed −2.3% and the S&P 500 about −2% (AP, 19 Nov).
The prior brief carried a 200K jobless-claims consensus (Admiral Markets). The print was 203,000, above it (MLQ, 19 Nov).
The prior brief listed Anthropic’s first Nasdaq trading day for Thursday at the $83 IPO price. It traded and closed at $97.17 (Forbes, 19 Nov).
The prior brief listed Walmart fiscal Q3 before the open. It reported as scheduled, beating and raising guidance (Walmart 8-K, 19 Nov).
The prior brief said whether the ~2% Nasdaq futures gap would survive the open was unresolved. It did not; no direction had been called.
